keyFindings.description: authWhoami (routes/router.go:470-476) answers 503 EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE for every eventHead error: the new unproven case (errEventHeadUnproven) and also a failed database or horizon-pool read (writerFloor's error, events.go:188, :196). This hides an error. The server answers EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE only for the unproven case and a different code for a failed read; the app retries only EVENT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE without limit and every other error on its bounded rule; with a test of each on the server and in the app (the architect's requirement).

writePersisted sets persistedAt only on success. After a failed write, every later observation is due again (h.safe > h.persistedSafe, persistedAt old), so the persist write runs every 10-250 ms instead of at most once a second, synchronously on the observing goroutine (the relay, the hub or a Safe/Await caller), each up to horizonPersistTimeout (2 s). Set persistedAt on failure too.

The generation is checked only after the persist write ran. If a Reset (a truncated log) falls between the decision at :555 and the write, or a pre-reset observation is proven after the new log has refilled past its id, persistHorizonSQL pairs the old log's H with the new row's created_at, Persisted trusts it, and writerFloor's fallback can answer an id that is not final in the new log. Reset path only (e2e seed). Check the generation under h.mu immediately before the write, and do not write when it moved.
